requirement: Rebuild the sphere material and internal lightning using the same already-working WebGL particle emitter engine, in compliance with Synestra procedures; no second engine/server/canvas.

implementation.single_engine: One WebGL emitterProgram and emitterBuffer drive all four uPass modes; one canvas and one WebGL context
implementation.pass_0: Optional extra VFX sparks, plasma, vortex or eruption; controlled by preset and intensity
implementation.pass_1: Sphere volume/surface formed from 3D golden-angle sampling, slow 3D-like projection and glowing sprites
implementation.pass_2: Internal electrical emission built from 24-point segments per bolt, temporal bursts, random directions, forked sections and depth attenuation
implementation.pass_3: Compact 3D-projected nucleus GPU emission; source power follows independent coreLight 0..500%, radius follows separate coreSize
implementation.render_order: Original soft legacy sphere underpainting/backdrop then shell, arcs, nucleus and optional sparks from same GPU point-sprite program with two luminance passes each
implementation.fallback: If emitter program fails to link, base sphere and its original arcs remain fully visible; no forced visual break
implementation.controls: Existing 38 native controls, no duplicate backend, no added platform connection, preserve shell visibility 0 as energy-only
implementation.user_interface: R151 unified VFX engine labeled in existing lab

initial_root_causes: Original 0-opacity emitter-uniform condition had to explicitly write zero
